transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Hi, yeah, thank you for seeing me. I, um, I guess the main reason I finally made this appointment—which actually took me a while to do because I kept
Do you avoid social situations because you’re afraid people will judge or embarrass you?
Um, no, not really at all, actually. I mean, I don't think I've ever really worried too much about people judging me? If anything, I'm usually the
Have you been having panic attacks?
Panic attacks? No, um, no, definitely not. Like, I've seen people have them—my roommate actually had one last semester right before our midterms, and it looked completely terrifying,
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try to ignore them?
Unwanted thoughts? Um, like, bad ones? No, I don't think so. I mean, my brain is definitely always on, like it never really shuts up, if that
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
Depressed? Um, no, not really. I mean, I get stressed, obviously, because college is just a lot right now. Like, last week I was super overwhelmed
Did your anxiety start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

A specific event? Um, I don't really think so? Like, there wasn't one big horrible thing that happened, you know? It's not like I went through a terrible breakup or failed a massive class or something dramatic like that. I guess you could say just starting college was a big change, because obviously moving into a dorm and having to figure out how to be a real person and manage a syllabus all by yourself is a lot. But it wasn't like a switch flipped after one bad day. 

It's honestly more like... just this constant thing where little things keep piling up. Like, I'll have a reading due, and then I need to do laundry, and then I realize I forgot to email my advisor back, and it just kind of snowballs into this big ball of stress. I feel like I've kind of always been a little bit like this, just constantly running a million miles a minute and trying to keep up. So, yeah, no, not one specific event, just kind of the general chaos of everything going on all at once, I guess
Do you find yourself worrying about a lot of different things, not just school?
Um, other things? Not really, no. I wouldn't say I'm a "worrier" in general. Like, my mom is a huge worrier, she's
Is this stress making it harder for you to keep up with school or daily life?

Um, yeah, I mean, it definitely does make things harder, for sure. Like, obviously school is the main thing right now, but it's not just classes. I do some freelance graphic design stuff on the side, just to build my portfolio and make a little extra cash for, you know, coffee and art supplies and stuff. And it's actually been kind of a disaster lately. I've actually lost a couple of small freelance contracts because I just... I couldn't get the final files sent over on time, or I'd forget a key detail the client asked for, and they just felt like they couldn't rely on me to follow through cleanly. Which sucks, because I know I can do the work, it's just the execution part that gets messy. 

And then there was this big portfolio competition last month that I was so excited about. I had all these great concepts sketched out, but I missed the submission deadline because I got the dates mixed up in my head and thought I had another week. It was so frustrating. And it's bleeding into my social life, too, honestly. I have friends in my program who are super talented, and we always talk about collaborating on projects, but lately I can tell they're kind of hesitant to work with me. Like, they'll say they love my ideas, which is nice, but when it comes time to actually divide up the work and set deadlines, they get this look, like they're worried I'm going to drop the ball and leave them hanging. So yeah, it's definitely affecting things outside of just, like, studying for exams. It just feels like I'm constantly scrambling to keep all these plates spinning, and a lot of them are crashing right now.
Did you have these same kinds of problems with staying organized, meeting deadlines, or forgetting things when you were a child?

Oh, yeah, definitely. I mean, it goes way, way back. Like, I remember even when I was little, in elementary school, my teachers were always writing notes on my report cards about it. It was never that I couldn't do the work, it was always stuff like, "She rushes through her worksheets," or "She doesn't read the directions carefully." I'd just want to get it done, you know? So I'd speed through and make all these silly mistakes. And then during group work, they'd say I was always talking over my classmates or just being too loud. I just got so excited about whatever we were doing, I couldn't wait my turn to speak. 

And at home, it was a whole other thing. Homework was always such a battle. My parents literally had to sit right next to me at the kitchen table every single night. Because if they didn't, I'd just... wander off. Like, I'd get up to get a glass of water, and then I'd see my dog and start playing with him, and then I'd remember a toy I wanted to find, and twenty minutes later my mom would find me in my room building Legos when I was supposed to be doing math. I just could not sit still and finish one thing before starting another. So they had to be there to constantly redirect me, like, "Okay, back to the worksheet, look at question number three." It was exhausting for them, I'm sure, and it was so frustrating for me because I felt like I was trying, but my brain just kept hopping to the next shiny thing. So yeah, it's definitely not a new thing, it's just that now I don't have my mom sitting next to me to keep me on track, you know?
